name: Patan Patola
summary: Double-ikat silk woven by the Salvi family of Patan, with every colour tied into the warp and weft before weaving. The geometric patterns are treated as family heirlooms rather than seasonal designs.
highlights: Double-ikat resist dyeing on warp and weft
Geometric and floral patterns tied before weaving
A heirloom textile associated with Gujarat's mercantile trade
image_alt: Detail of a patola cloth from Gujarat, late 18th or early 19th century
popular_time: October–March, during the cooler weaving season

name: Ajrakh block printing
summary: Indigo and madder resist printing practised by Khatri artisans in Ajrakhpur. Patterns are built up through repeated washing, dyeing and hand-carved blocks.
highlights: Patterns shared across Kutch and Sindh
image_alt: Kutch artisans holding up an Ajrakh block-printed cloth in indigo and red
popular_time: October–March, when the printed cloth dries evenly

name: Bandhani
summary: Tie-and-dye cloth in which thousands of tiny knots resist the dye before the fabric is opened. Each pattern is named for the motif it forms, from dots to flowers.
popular_time: October–March, during the wedding and festival season

name: Garba
summary: A circular devotional dance performed around a lit shrine during Navratri, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023. Claps, turns and call-and-response songs mark the rhythm.
highlights: Community circles that grow through the night

name: Dandiya Raas
summary: A stick dance performed in paired circles, with wooden dandiya struck in time to the music. It is a fixture of Navratri nights alongside Garba.
highlights: Rhythm kept by striking the sticks

name: Tippani
summary: A work-song dance from Saurashtra in which women strike the ground with wooden rods as they compact earth for building. The rhythm of the labour becomes the rhythm of the dance.
highlights: Wooden rods struck against the ground
A dance rooted in building labour

name: Navratri
summary: Nine nights of worship, music and dance dedicated to the goddess. Neighbourhoods gather around Garba and Dandiya Raas through the night.
popular_time: September–October, nine nights around the new moon

name: Uttarayan
summary: The kite festival marking the sun's northward journey, celebrated from rooftops and terraces. Paper kites fill the sky while neighbours share undhiyu and sweets.
highlights: Undhiyu and sweets shared with neighbours

name: Rann Utsav
summary: A winter festival on the white salt flats of the Rann. Craft markets, music and desert excursions run through the season.
highlights: Full-moon walks on the salt flats

name: Bhavai
summary: A travelling folk-theatre form in which performers move between villages with improvised dialogue, music and social satire. Open-ground shows use stock characters with live tabla and sarangi accompaniment.
highlights: Accompanied by the tabla and sarangi
popular_time: October–March, at village fairs and festival nights

name: Dayro
summary: A gathering for folk storytelling and singing, led by a narrator who moves between song, verse and spoken tales. Dayros often run late into the night at village and town events.
popular_time: October–March, at community gatherings and festivals

name: Gujarati cinema
summary: The regional film tradition of Gujarat, spanning early black-and-white productions to contemporary independent features. Its songs and dialogue draw on the state's folk theatre and oral storytelling.
popular_time: Year-round; festival screenings peak in winter
